sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Luned is a maid in the stories of King Arthur. She served the lady of the Fountain, whose name was Laudine. Luned told the young knight Owein how to defeat the lady's guardian. She then helped him win the lady for his wife. Later she let the knights of the Round Table know that Owein had abandoned his wife. She also worked to bring the two together again. Some of her powers suggest a fairy origin. The Breton name for such fairies is Korrigans.

okr.objective: Record the part Luned plays in the tale of Owein and the Lady of the Fountain.
